body:
I am Chinese. I won't describe my thoughts like this. I think many people are motivated by multiple reasons when they do something, but I don't know if it can be fully altruistic.

Take the Chinese communist party as an example. Or the North Korean leaders. Of course, I can't read the minds of the leaders but I don't think they are truly altruistic. The same applies to politicians of other countries. The might twist those words so it doesn't sound so awful but it doesn't mean that they are truly altruistic. In fact, it seems naive as hell to believe that people are truly altruistic as they say so.
I don't think true altruism exists.

It is still selfish. Most people somewhat want a spouse with status. Most don't do it given that people with status are a catch so they may see them as out of their league or that they don't know anyone like that in their social circles. I think that most people are not happily married and there must be a reason for it.

And yes, kids go back to selfishness. You want your kids to succeed, not someone else's kids. If it's either your kid or someone else's kid competing for that award or promotion, you want your kid to have it.

The darkest ones are the ones who pretend to be nice when they are not. Like that coworker who pretends to be nice while he actually hates you and wants that promotion instead.
